Test a weighted combination using inverse error to see if giving more weight to lower‑error models improves over the robust mean, given the unstable ranking.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable ranking; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust weighted combination may improve over mean.
Test a robust median combination to see if it beats the mean in this trend‑dominated, unstable‑ranking series.
The series has unstable ranking and strong trend; a per‑horizon weighted combo may capture horizon‑specific best models.
The series is trend‑dominated and ranking unstable; a robust DBA combination may outperform simple mean by reducing bias from correlated models.
The series has unstable ranking; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting may capture horizon‑specific wins.
Test a simple mean over the stable pool4 (trend‑dominated, unstable ranking) to see if a reduced robust subset beats the full‑mean baseline.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a simpler robust mean over a stable subset (pool1) may improve over the global mean by reducing influence of highly variable models.
test a robust median on a stable, cross‑group pool

decision.justification: Selected 'mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 1.0. Series context: trend strength 0.9897 and seasonal strength 0.4836; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.092); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.35.
